newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up on dry, cool weather outlook.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up on dry, cool weather outlook.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on some outlooks for continued dry weather next week in the U.S. Midwest plus indications for cool temperatures to soon slip into the soybean growing region, traders said.
"It's still dry and there is some concern about that," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Meteorologists early Friday noted the likelihood that only light showers would fall in the Midwest in the near term. There had been ideas that Hurricane Fran may leave crop- enhancing rain in her wake but such forecasts were altered Friday to indicate dry conditions would generally prevail.
Rumors circulated that China was seeking or had bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 100,000 tonnes of soymeal.
Commercial bull spreading in soybeans helped magnify the talk and net commercial buying of soymeal further fueled the rumors about Chinese demand.
New crop November soybeans closed at $8.00 per bushel, a key resistance level on charts. "The $8.00 close is bullish psychologically," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Soybeans closed three to nine cents per bushel higher, with September up nine at $8.24-1/4 a bushel.

Term Commodities, Tenco Inc and Continental Grain each bull spread roughly one half million bushels of September/December, traders said. Refco Inc bought eight million bushels of November, Rosenthal Collins bought four million November and ADM Investor Services bought 2.5 million November, the traders said.
In the soymeal pit, Continental Grain bought 800 lots of December and bought 400 lots of October, sources said.
The market shrugged off bearish input from a couple of private crop estimates.
The Leslie/ADM elevator survey released early Friday indicated 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.24 billion bushels, down from USDA's outlook for 2.3 billion.
Traders said Sparks Companies pegged 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.276 billion bushels.
Traders said Friday's estimates were bearish for soybean futures because there have been some private outlooks placing the crop down to 2.1 billion.
USDA Wednesday is slated to release its September crop production report.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 47,000 contracts, up from 41,518 Thursday.

Action in soybean options also was viewed as supportive to futures. ADM Investor Services bought 1,500 November $8.25 calls and sold 1,500 November $8.50 calls at six cents, the traders said. Produce Grain bought 850 November $7.75 calls and sold 850 November $8.25 calls at 20-1/2 to 21 cents.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 26,000 contracts, up from 21,603 Thursday.
